rules.text: Freehold Property: The property is understood to be held on a freehold basis. Your legal adviser should confirm the tenure, that vacant possession will be available on completion, and whether the title is subject to any restrictive covenants, easements, rights of way, or other matters that could affect the use, enjoyment, marketability, or value of the property. Your legal adviser should also confirm whether there are any estate rent charges, maintenance contributions, management company obligations, or other ongoing financial liabilities associated with the property. Where the property forms part of a managed estate or private development, enquiries should be made regarding the management arrangements, service or estate charges, planned maintenance works, and any outstanding financial liabilities or disputes.

Leasehold Property: Your legal adviser should also confirm the amount of any ground rent, service charges, reserve fund contributions, and whether these are reasonable. They should investigate the lease for any onerous covenants, restrictions, or unusual obligations that could affect the property's value, marketability, or future sale. Enquiries should be made of the landlord or managing agent to establish whether there are any outstanding service charges, planned major works, disputes, or significant future expenditure. Confirmation should also be obtained that appropriate buildings insurance and management arrangements are in place.

Share of Freehold Property: Where the property is held with a share of the freehold, your legal adviser should confirm the ownership structure, the remaining lease term, rights and obligations under the lease, responsibility for repairs and maintenance, service charges, reserve fund contributions, management arrangements, any restrictive covenants, and whether there are any planned major works or ongoing disputes affecting the building.

Flying Freehold: Where the property includes or is affected by a flying freehold, your legal adviser should confirm the extent of the flying freehold and ensure that adequate rights of support, shelter, protection, access for inspection, maintenance and repair are contained within the title. They should also confirm that there are no restrictions which could adversely affect the property's marketability or mortgageability, and that suitable indemnity insurance or other legal protection is available where required.

Private Road: The property is accessed via a private road or shared access. Your legal adviser should confirm ownership, rights of access, maintenance responsibilities, and any financial obligations associated with its upkeep.

Rights of Way: The property may be affected by rights of way or other third-party rights. Your legal adviser should confirm whether any such rights exist and advise on any implications for the use, enjoyment, marketability, and value of the property.

Party Wall: The property shares one or more walls or structural elements with neighbouring property. Your legal adviser should explain any legal implications, including those arising under the Party Wall etc. Act 1996, where applicable, particularly if you intend to undertake structural alterations or certain repair works.

Tenanted Property: The property appears to be, or may be, occupied by a tenant. Your legal adviser should confirm whether the property will be sold with vacant possession on completion and advise on any tenancy agreements or occupiers' rights that may affect the purchase.

General Legal Enquiries: Your legal adviser should raise any additional enquiries considered appropriate following review of this report, the contract documentation, and the property title. The matters identified above arise from a visual inspection only and are intended to assist your legal adviser during the conveyancing process. They should not be regarded as a comprehensive list of legal enquiries, and your legal adviser should make any additional investigations considered appropriate.
